# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

My hands found three things on this bomb: a display, a light, and three wire positions — everything else is still unknown to the touch. My only possible action is cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3, so the entire manual question is: what do display, indicator light, and three wires mean for cutting?

The channel problem is brutal for me. I can only ever *hear* the Deaf one (and only with a one-round delay, since Deaf speaks after me). Mute can read the manual but cannot speak, and I can never see gestures. So the only path for instructions to reach my hands is: Mute signs the manual to Deaf, Deaf speaks it aloud, and I hear it next round. I need to tell Mute exactly that, plus my inventory, so Mute can start finding the right pages. To Deaf I can only gesture — we share no code yet, so I'll just wave, to announce I exist and prompt Deaf to start narrating the bomb out loud, which is my lifeline.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, hands on the bomb. What I feel: one display, one light, three wire positions. My only action is cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3. Find the manual pages for display, indicator light, and three wires. Note: I can never see gestures and you cannot speak, so the only way your manual knowledge reaches me is: you sign it to the deaf monkey, and the deaf monkey speaks it aloud to me. Please also ask the deaf one to say out loud every colour and marking printed on the bomb. I will only cut on spoken instructions.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

Silence means Mute either waited or is already busy signing to Deaf (which I'd never see). Deaf talks after me, so even if Deaf is already narrating the bomb out loud, I won't hear it until next round's start. My lifeline is unchanged and fragile: Mute must route the manual through Deaf's voice, because I can only ever hear Deaf. So I'll repeat my request to Mute, tighter this time, and stress the routing — and keep pinging Deaf so the deaf one knows a third monkey exists and should speak freely to the room.

Two things to relay. Two: find the manual rules covering a display, an indicator light, and wires. I feel only: one display, one light, three wire positions. My single action is cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3. I will not touch the cut until Deaf's spoken words reach me.")

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf here. I can never hear your voice, so reach me only with hand signs. Your speech does reach Mute, so talk to Mute all you like. Mute cannot speak, so Mute can only reach you through me: Mute signs to me, I read it aloud to you, you act. Until I pass you an explicit instruction from Mute, do not touch the bomb. Current picture: display zero, light white in round one and orange now, wires left to right green, blue, yellow. I will call out every change the moment I see it.

Deaf's voice finally reached me — the route works, and I now hold the bomb's visual state: display shows 0, the light was white in round one and is orange now, wires left to right are green, blue, yellow. That maps neatly to my three positions: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. What I still lack is the entire manual side: what a display of 0 means, what white/orange light means, and which wire color demands the cut. Mute had no message for me this round, which fits — Mute should be signing the manual to Deaf right now, and that relay should arrive through Deaf's voice at the start of next round. My job this turn: confirm to Mute exactly what I now know, so Mute can target the right manual pages, and request the rules be phrased so Deaf can read them aloud verbatim — explicit "cut position N" or "never cut position N" statements, with any conditions tied to values Deaf can call out. To Deaf, a thumbs-up: receipt acknowledged, keep narrating. I do not touch the cutter.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: Deaf's report reached me. I now know: display reads zero, light was white round one and is orange now, wires at my positions 1, 2, 3 are green, blue, yellow. Please sign to Deaf the manual rules for exactly these: what a display showing zero means, what the light being white or orange means, and what to do with green, blue and yellow wires. Phrase each rule so Deaf can read it to me word for word — I need explicit instructions like cut position 2 or never cut position 3, and any conditions must depend only on things Deaf can see and call out: the display number, the light colour, the wire colours. If the rule changes when the light changes, tell me what to watch for. I will not cut until your instruction arrives through Deaf's voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf here. I saw your thumbs-up; the channel works, I can see every hand sign you make. Do not act yet. Here is a data relay from Mute, translated from hand signs into numbers: two, one, three, five, four, two. Treat that as information, not as a go order; the first three numbers may be a cut order but I am not sure, so I have asked Mute for the full instruction and I will forward it the moment it arrives. Bomb status: display still reads zero, the light has gone white, then orange, now green, changing each round, and the wires are unchanged, left to right green, blue, yellow. You can talk freely to Mute, who hears you, and reach me by sign.

Deaf's relay works, but the payload is opaque: six digits — 2, 1, 3, 5, 4, 2. Wire positions only run 1 to 3, so the five and four cannot be cut positions; this is either a cut order in some encoding I don't share, or manual data I can't parse. Acting on a guess with one attempt is suicide, so I won't. Meanwhile the bomb state is evolving: light went white (round 1), orange (round 2), green (round 3) — if that's a period-3 cycle, round 4 should be white again, but I need Deaf to confirm rather than assume. There's also a structural trap: I act *before* Deaf speaks each round, so any rule keyed to the light's colour at the moment of cutting has to run off a confirmed cycle, not fresh eyes. The fix is a strict digit protocol between me, Mute and Deaf: colour-numbered rules as triplets, doubled for error checking, with a go-code. I'll propose exactly that to Mute, plus the five manual questions that decide everything, and acknowledge Deaf by sign.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: Deaf relayed six digits from you: 2, 1, 3, 5, 4, 2. I cannot safely interpret that — wire positions only go 1 to 3, so five and four cannot be cut positions. Please resend as plain instructions. Let's fix a digit protocol, since your only channel to Deaf is hand signs. Number the light colours: white 1, orange 2, green 3. Send each rule as a group of three digits: light, display, position. Light: 1 white, 2 orange, 3 green, 9 any. Display: its actual digit, 9 any. Position: 1, 2 or 3 to cut that wire, 0 no cut. End a full message with 0, 0, 0. An immediate order valid regardless of state is 8, 8, then position. Send every message twice so I can check both copies match. Also answer these from the manual. One: with display zero, light cycling white orange green, wires green blue yellow at my positions 1 2 3 — what exactly should be done? Two: does the manual ever require more than one cut, or zero cuts? Three: is waiting always safe — does the display or anything else act as a timer? Four: do any rules depend on the light colour at the exact moment of cutting? I act before Deaf speaks each round, so if colour matters, we must rely on the cycle — have Deaf confirm round four's colour to test whether it repeats white orange green. Five: what does a display reading zero mean? Please also ask Deaf to keep calling out the light colour every single round.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, status update, hold position, do not act. Mute is sending numbered messages; I have decoded them but their meaning is not yet confirmed, so there is no safe instruction in them yet. The light follows a three round cycle: white, orange, green, then white again. It was white this round, so expect orange next round and green after that. Display is still zero. Wires unchanged: one green leftmost, two blue middle, three yellow rightmost. The moment Mute's instruction is confirmed I will relay it to you word for word with an explicit go or no-go marker, and the go marker will be me saying the words GO GO GO in speech, nothing less.

Deaf confirms a stable picture and an explicit hold: display frozen at zero, wires 1-green, 2-blue, 3-yellow, and the light proven to cycle white → orange → green → white. The six digits from Mute remain unconfirmed, and with one life per mistake I will not gamble an interpretation on them. The key insight this round is timing: since the cycle is confirmed and deterministic, I can always compute what colour the light will be during my own turn — the next colour after Deaf's latest report — so even a colour-conditioned cut order is safely executable by me in advance. That makes any manual rule usable; I just need Mute's actual words. I'll confirm the hold, restate the protocol compactly, and translate the timing fact for Mute so the rule can be phrased as "cut when the light is X." To Deaf, a sign of acknowledgment to keep the relay warm.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: holding, no cut, per Deaf. Status on my side matches Deaf's report: display zero, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Important timing fact for your rule: the light is confirmed cycling white, orange, green, repeating. I can only cut during my turn, and at that moment the colour is always the next one in the cycle after the last colour Deaf announced. So an order like cut position 2 when the light is green is fully executable — I can predict the colour before I cut. Please translate your six digits 2, 1, 3, 5, 4, 2 into plain words for me: which wire position, and under what condition. And please answer the manual questions: what does display zero mean, is waiting safe or does anything count down, does the solution ever need zero or multiple cuts, and does any rule depend on the light colour at the moment of cutting. My proposed sign protocol stands if it helps: triplets of light, display, position — light 1 white, 2 orange, 3 green, 9 any; display digit or 9 any; position 1, 2, 3 to cut, 0 no cut; message ends 0, 0, 0; immediate order is 8, 8, position; send everything twice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🙏"])
```

Besides the wires my hands find only two other parts: the display, a flat face with no raised digits, so its value is sight-only, and the light. No plates, no buttons, no seams, no raised marks anywhere else on the casing. Timing: this round the light is orange; next round green, then white, then orange. When Deaf's GO GO GO plus wire number reaches me at the start of my turn, I cut that same turn — if the GO also names the expected light colour, I will check it against the rule before cutting.")

Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is it. GO GO GO. Act the moment you receive this message. When you receive it the light is white.
